title: Affine strict-transform chart formula
statement:
Let $f:A\to B$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings, let $I\subseteq A$ be an ideal, and let $a\in I$. Put $b=f(a)$ and $J=IB$. With the map $\sigma_a:C_a(A,B,I)\to B[J/b]$ of [def-nagata-strict-chart-to-extended-blowup-chart] and the quotient ring $C_a^{\mathrm{st}}(A,B,I)$ of [def-nagata-strict-transform-chart-ring], the constructed comparison
$$\overline\sigma_a:C_a^{\mathrm{st}}(A,B,I)\longrightarrow B[J/b]$$
of [def-nagata-strict-transform-chart-comparison] is a ring equivalence (with this specified forward homomorphism).

proof.text: Write $C=C_a(A,B,I)$, $T=\Gamma_{(a)}(C)$, $D=B[J/b]$, and $q:C\to C/T$ for the quotient map. By [def-nagata-strict-transform-chart-ring], the source is precisely $C/T$. By [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient], $q$ is surjective with kernel $T$. The definition [def-nagata-strict-transform-chart-comparison] gives the ring homomorphism $g=\overline\sigma_a:C/T\to D$ with $g(q(c))=\sigma_a(c)$ for every $c\in C$. These are the actual quotient and induced map, so it suffices to show that $g$ has a ring-homomorphism inverse.

proof.text: For injectivity, take $u,v\in C/T$ with $g(u)=g(v)$. Lift them through the surjective $q$ to $c,d\in C$. Then $\sigma_a(c-d)=g(u)-g(v)=0$. The kernel equality of [lemma-nagata-strict-chart-map-kernel] says exactly that $c-d\in T$. Since $\ker q=T$ by [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient], we have $u-v=q(c-d)=0$, hence $u=v$. The identity $gq=\sigma_a$ used here is the defining identity in [def-nagata-strict-transform-chart-comparison].

source.place: Proof: surjectivity, kernel, and first isomorphism theorem, expanded on quotient representatives; quotient rings as in Stacks Tag 00AR, algebra.tex, section-rings-basic, item-quotient-ring

proof.text: For any $y\in D$, [lemma-nagata-strict-chart-map-surjective] supplies $c\in C$ with $\sigma_a(c)=y$. By the defining identity in [def-nagata-strict-transform-chart-comparison], $g(q(c))=y$. Thus $g$ is surjective as well as injective.

proof.text: For $y\in D$, let $h(y)$ be its unique preimage under $g$, whose existence and uniqueness were proved in steps 2 and 3. Then $gh=\mathrm{id}_D$ and $hg=\mathrm{id}_{C/T}$. To check the ring structure, use that the induced map $g$ in [def-nagata-strict-transform-chart-comparison] is a ring homomorphism: $g(h(y)+h(z))=y+z=g(h(y+z))$ and $g(h(y)h(z))=yz=g(h(yz))$. Injectivity gives the additive and multiplicative laws for $h$; likewise $g(0)=0=g(h(0))$ and $g(1)=1=g(h(1))$ give $h(0)=0$ and $h(1)=1$. Therefore $h$ is the inverse ring homomorphism and the specified $g=\overline\sigma_a$ is a ring equivalence.

blueprint_notes.text:
**Status.** Bypassed by the formalized route: the strict transform is
supplied by the API of
`WeilConjectures/Compactification/StrictTransform.lean` —
`AlgebraicGeometry.strictTransform`, its closed immersion
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.IdealSheafData.isClosedImmersion_pullbackLift_blowup_comap`,
and the pullback square
`AlgebraicGeometry.isPullback_strictTransformOpen` — so the
strict-transform chart rings and their cocycle are never assembled by hand.

blueprint_update.statement: The constructed comparison $\overline\sigma_a$ is a ring equivalence.

proof.text:
The map $\sigma_a$ is surjective and its kernel is precisely the ideal by
which the source was quotiented. The first isomorphism theorem therefore
makes $\overline\sigma_a$ bijective and identifies its inverse ring
structure, so it is a ring equivalence.
